opportunities.title: Research apps and databases after funding ends
opportunities.narrowed_scope: See B-S2a: research/teaching tools killed by officially retired runtimes (Flash, Java applets, Google Fusion Tables)
target_users: university RSE/DH labs holding legacy project estates (e.g. King's Digital Lab)
opportunities.payer: institutional subscriptions (TAIR), private funders (Wellcome), university lab budgets (KDL); none found for a third-party tool
opportunities.maintainer: university RSE/DH labs, spun-out nonprofits (Phoenix Bioinformatics), consortia (Alliance of Genome Resources)

cases.case: FlyBase NIH grant terminated May 2025
TAIR moved to subscriptions after NSF funding ended 2013
King's Digital Lab inherited ~100 legacy DH projects
PDBj SFAS web service suspended Feb 2024 for lack of IT staff
GBC: 32 of 52 Global Core Biodata Resources US-funded

opportunities.consequence_of_inaction: Curated core resources lose staff and updates; long-tail tools go dark (~28% of omics tool URLs already unreachable).
opportunities.strongest_alternative: KDL Archiving & Sustainability process plus Endings static-site principles; for large resources, funder rescue and subscription models
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Large resources need money, not a new tool, and KDL reports many PIs chose to let finished projects be archived rather than kept running.
opportunities.falsifier: Survey KDL/Endings-style legacy estates: if most projects either archive cleanly or convert static with existing tools at low cost, no gap remains.

demand.basis: Strong behavioural evidence for funding large resources (FlyBase, TAIR, GBC), none that target users want a new solution

international.basis: Direct cases in NA, EU, Asia (SFAS) but Asia evidence is one notice

innovation.basis: KDL and Endings already cover the core job manually

theme.basis: Grant expiry is not a dead technology

ai.basis: AI optional for code reading; static conversion is deterministic

feasibility.basis: Feasible only on a narrowed slice

sustainability.basis: Services are paid for (TAIR, KDL SLA); tools are not

opportunities.title: Research and teaching tools killed by retired runtimes (Flash, Java applets, Fusion Tables)
opportunities.narrowed_scope: Legacy academic simulations and data apps that stopped working because Flash, Java applets or Google Fusion Tables were retired, held by labs/education projects with legacy estates
target_users: educational simulation projects with legacy sims (e.g. PhET)
university DH/RSE labs with Flash/applet-era projects
opportunities.payer: donations and foundation grants (PhET); lab budgets; none found for a third-party tool
opportunities.maintainer: project teams; emulator communities (Ruffle, CheerpJ vendor Leaning Technologies)

cases.case: PhET Flash sims stopped 1 Jan 2021; Java sims via CheerpJ with missing features
Google Fusion Tables discontinued, data deleted after 3 Mar 2020 (global service)

opportunities.consequence_of_inaction: Interactive research and teaching tools stay unusable or partially working under emulators.
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Ruffle (Flash), CheerpJ (Java applets), manual HTML5 rewrites (PhET)
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Mature emulators already run much Flash/applet content; the residual gap for research tools is unmeasured.
opportunities.resurrection_anchor: Adobe Flash Player (EOL 2020/2021); Java browser applets; Google Fusion Tables (discontinued 2019, data deleted 2020)
opportunities.falsifier: Take 20 public academic Flash/Java-applet tools; if >=80% already run fully under Ruffle/CheerpJ or have been rewritten, drop.

demand.basis: PhET spends donations on conversion; no evidence beyond one organisation

international.basis: NA case plus a globally retired runtime (structural generalisation)

innovation.basis: Ruffle/CheerpJ partly cover the job; gap unmeasured

theme.basis: Officially retired runtime directly causes the loss

ai.basis: AI translation of applet logic plausible, checkable against emulator output; unproven

feasibility.basis: Open-licensed legacy sims and open emulators available now

demo.basis: Before/after on a real dead simulation is visual

opportunities.title: Small-platform shutdown window
target_users: operators of small community platforms near shutdown
opportunities.payer: none found for small operators; large operators self-fund export (Glitch/Fastly, Yahoo)
opportunities.maintainer: volunteers (ArchiveTeam); receiving platforms build importers in large cases

cases.case: Cohost shutdown 2024-2025, delayed for ArchiveTeam
Glitch ended hosting 8 Jul 2025 with code export and redirects
Yahoo!ブログ closure 2019 with official migration tool to rival blogs (large platform)
Xiami closure 2021, playlists to NetEase/QQ (large platform)

opportunities.consequence_of_inaction: Read-only copies usually survive via ArchiveTeam, but community relationships of small platforms are lost.
opportunities.strongest_alternative: ArchiveTeam + Wayback for read-only copies; operator export/redirects; rival importers
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Small operators close because they have no money (Cohost $17k/month deficit), so the moment the tool is needed is the moment no one can pay.
opportunities.falsifier: Find any small operator or funder that paid for community transfer at shutdown; if none, the drop stands.

demand.basis: Volunteer and operator behaviour demonstrated; no WTP for a tool

international.basis: NA small cases; Asia only large-platform cases; EU only regulation (snippet)

innovation.basis: ArchiveTeam, exports and rival importers cover the core job

theme.basis: Defined as before shutdown: prevention, not revival

feasibility.basis: Technically simple; real data access is the risk

demo.basis: Story clear but demo needs a cooperating platform

opportunities.title: Disappearing small and scholar-led journals
opportunities.narrowed_scope: See B-T3a; T3 as a whole fails the theme gate
target_users: editors of small scholar-led OA journals
opportunities.payer: preservation networks and libraries (CLOCKSS, IA, DOAJ, PKP) absorb costs; journals pay nothing
opportunities.maintainer: CLOCKSS, Portico, PKP PN, Internet Archive, DOAJ (JASPER)

cases.case: 57 of 174 vanished OA journals (Laakso et al.)
52 vanished journals in Europe & Central Asia
23 South Asia + 18 East Asia & Pacific vanished; Indonesia LIS rescue project (snippet)
17 Latin America & Caribbean; 6 MENA

opportunities.consequence_of_inaction: About 28% of DOI-registered articles remain without confirmed preservation, risking broken citation chains.
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Project JASPER + PKP Preservation Network + CLOCKSS (free for eligible small journals)
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Free infrastructure exists and uptake is still low (~100 invited, 32 preserved), so the bottleneck is participation, not technology.
opportunities.falsifier: Already largely falsified as a tooling gap by JASPER uptake data; would revive only if a non-participation cause solvable by tooling were shown.

demand.basis: Strong secondary quantitative evidence (Laakso, Eve); no evidence journals want a new tool

international.basis: All regions in one dataset; per-region independent evidence thinner

innovation.basis: JASPER, PKP PN, CLOCKSS cover the core job

theme.basis: Journals are not a dead technology

opportunities.title: Journals stranded on end-of-life OJS 2.x or surviving only in web archives
opportunities.narrowed_scope: Conditional: only if a count shows a material number of active journals still on OJS 2.x (excluded from PKP PN) or vanished journals recoverable from Wayback captures; otherwise drop
target_users: editors of journals still running OJS 2.x
opportunities.maintainer: none found beyond PKP upgrade documentation

cases.case: Indonesia LIS journal rescue project (snippet only)
OJS 2.x officially unsupported since 2021 (global software)

opportunities.consequence_of_inaction: Journals on OJS 2.x stay unpatched and outside free preservation networks.
opportunities.strongest_alternative: PKP OJS 2-to-3 upgrade path; Internet Archive Scholar
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: OJS 2.x is not the main reason journals vanish; Laakso and JASPER point to resources and awareness.
opportunities.falsifier: Count active OJS 2.x journals (version footers/PKP statistics); if fewer than a few hundred or most already in Keepers Registry, drop.

international.basis: OJS is deployed globally; structural generalisation only

innovation.basis: PKP upgrade path and IA Scholar partly cover

theme.basis: Retired tech exists but is not central to the loss; 3 would be a stretch

ai.basis: Metadata extraction from heterogeneous archives; GROBID baseline

feasibility.basis: Needs a real OJS 2.x instance or Wayback capture

opportunities.title: Heritage archive transfer when custodians cannot maintain
opportunities.narrowed_scope: See B-T4a; T4 as a whole fails the theme gate
opportunities.payer: foundations and agencies (Arcadia, Mellon, IMLS, NEH)
opportunities.maintainer: WSU Mukurtu team; institutional archives (BBAW for ELAR); communities

cases.case: Indigenous digital heritage projects 2002-2007 hit by outdated software and funding problems
ELDP/ELAR moved from SOAS London to BBAW Berlin with Arcadia grant (2021)
Mukurtu origins with Warumungu community, Australia
No protocol-governed archive case found; Hong Kong collection.news case is political (snippet)

opportunities.consequence_of_inaction: Community archives run on unsupported software or lose cultural access rules when moved.
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Mukurtu 4 with official migration tool; transfer to established archives (ELAR, PARADISEC)
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: The bottleneck may be governance and staffing, and a public copy would violate cultural protocols, so generic preservation is harmful here.
opportunities.falsifier: If most custodian transitions are handled by funders moving collections to institutional archives (ELAR model), no tooling gap exists.

demand.basis: Funders spend (Arcadia EUR 21M); no evidence for a new tool

international.basis: NA, EU, Oceania; no Asia protocol case

innovation.basis: Mukurtu and institutional archives cover the core job

theme.basis: Heritage is not a dead technology

opportunities.title: Community archives stranded on Mukurtu 3 / Drupal 7
opportunities.narrowed_scope: Customised Mukurtu 3 sites (Drupal 7, no longer supported) that the official stock-site migration tool does not cover, where cultural-protocol access rules must survive the move to Mukurtu 4
opportunities.payer: Mukurtu team already pays HeroDevs for Drupal 7 extended security support; foundations fund Mukurtu; none found for a third-party tool

cases.case: Mukurtu 3 on Drupal 7; HeroDevs contract ~1 year after Mukurtu 4; migration tool designed for stock sites
Mukurtu deployments in Australia (Warumungu origin)

opportunities.consequence_of_inaction: Customised sites keep running unpatched Drupal 7 after extended support ends, risking exposure of restricted cultural content.
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Official Mukurtu 4 migration tool plus direct support from the Mukurtu team
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: The number of customised Mukurtu 3 sites is unknown and may be small, and the funded Mukurtu team already offers custom migration help.
opportunities.resurrection_anchor: Drupal 7 (security support ended; per Drupal.org 5 Jan 2025, snippet) and Mukurtu CMS 3 (superseded by Mukurtu 4)
opportunities.falsifier: Count public Mukurtu 3 sites still live and ask the Mukurtu team what share need custom migration; if the official tool plus team support covers nearly all, drop.

demand.basis: Spending by the vendor (HeroDevs) demonstrated; community demand for an extra tool unknown

innovation.basis: Official tool covers stock sites; custom-site gap plausible but unmeasured

theme.basis: Officially retired Drupal 7 directly forces the migration

ai.basis: Access-matrix check is deterministic; AI only for reading custom modules

feasibility.basis: Requires building a synthetic Mukurtu 3 site

demo.basis: Before/after access matrix is visual but needs context
